_source: Wind Waker DUNGEON PROGRESSION - small keys, locked doors, the Big Key, dungeon map and compass, and the per-dungeon save state. Mined 2026-08-21 for the gcrip remake. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, both cited on every claim. (a) DECOMP: zeldaret/tww at Z:/memRip/sources/tww, read-only. Every 'src' string is a real file:line that was opened and read; paths are relative to that root. (b) DISC: the placement numbers were re-parsed straight out of the retail GZLE01 ISO's DZS/DZR chunks - STAG for the save slot, TGDR for doors, TRES for chests. The same numbers are already in the build's out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json (actor / params / rot / chunk=='TGDR' / chunk=='TRES'), and the two agree entry for entry. SCHEMA (designed for this system, deliberately NOT the story-step schema): _storage = the save layout; _stage_save_slots = every stage on the disc -> its save slot; _switch_numbers = how a switch id routes to storage; _doors = each door actor and how it decides to open; _items = small key / big key / map / compass; _chests = the tbox param layout; _dungeons = one entry per dungeon with its real door and chest placements; _not_determined = the honest gaps. A 'confidence' key appears wherever a claim is inferred rather than read straight out of code or data.

_storage.summary: Dungeon state does NOT live in the event-bit array. It lives in a separate 16-entry table of per-stage save blocks. Each block is one dSv_memBit_c (0x24 bytes) holding chests-opened, persistent switches, item-drop bits, rooms-visited, the small-key COUNT, and a 6-bit dungeon-item mask (map / compass / big key / boss-dead / heart-container-taken / boss-cutscene-seen).

fields.name: mTbox
fields.meaning: chest-opened bits, 32 chests per save slot

fields.name: mSwitch
fields.meaning: 128 persistent 'memory' switches per save slot - this is what a locked door sets when you unlock it, and what most dungeon puzzles latch

fields.name: mItem
fields.meaning: item-drop bits (a dropped pickup that must not respawn)
fields.note: the JUT_ASSERT in the source says 0<=i<64 while the array is only ONE u32. That mismatch is verbatim in the decomp. Treat as 32 usable bits.
fields.confidence: high on the code, the 64-vs-32 discrepancy is real and unexplained

fields.name: mVisitedRoom
fields.meaning: 64 room-visited bits - this is what fills in the dungeon map as you walk
fields.set_by: dMap_c::mapMoveAll() -> dComIfGs_onVisitedRoom(roomNo), skipped when the stage type is FF1 or SEA (src/d/d_map.cpp:1538-1541)

fields.name: mKeyNum
fields.meaning: SMALL KEY COUNT for this dungeon, clamped 0..99

dSv_memBit_c.init: dSv_memBit_c::init() zeroes all of it including mKeyNum and mDungeonItem (src/d/d_save.cpp:1054-1069)

dungeon_item_bits.src: include/d/d_save.h:630-637 (the enum) and include/d/d_save.h:656-673 (the named accessors)

2.name: BOSS_KEY
2.note: this IS the Big Key - there is no separate big-key variable anywhere

3.name: STAGE_BOSS_ENEMY
3.note: the dungeon boss is dead. This is the bit dComIfGs_onStageBossEnemy() writes; it is a per-stage save field, not an event bit.

table_of_slots.layout: dSv_save_c { dSv_player_c mPlayer @0x000 (0x380); dSv_memory_c mMemory[16] @0x380 (0x240); dSv_ocean_c mOcean @0x5C0; dSv_event_c mEvent @0x624; dSv_reserve_c mReserve @0x724 }  // sizeof 0x778
table_of_slots.note: dSv_memory_c is a 0x24-byte wrapper containing exactly one dSv_memBit_c (include/d/d_save.h:719-729)
table_of_slots.live_copy: dSv_info_c also holds ONE live block, mMemory @0x778, plus mDan @0x79C and mZone[32] @0x7A8 (include/d/d_save.h:973-984). All the dComIfGs_ accessors without a stageNo argument hit the live block.

current_slot_selection.how: The slot number is a field in the stage's STAG chunk (stage.dzs). It is not a lookup on the stage name.
current_slot_selection.decode: dStage_stagInfo_GetSaveTbl(stag) = (stag->mProp >> 1) & 0x7F   // mProp is byte 0x09 of the 0x20-byte STAG record
current_slot_selection.sibling_field: dStage_stagInfo_ChkKeyDisp(stag) = stag->mProp & 1  -> 'this stage displays the small-key counter'. See include/d/d_stage.h:1019-1021. It gates the whole key commit path (src/d/d_meter.cpp:5167).
current_slot_selection.store: dStage_Delete(): stageNo = GetSaveTbl(stag); dComIfGs_putSave(stageNo)  (src/d/d_stage.cpp:2255-2256). Also on a manual save: src/d/d_menu_save.cpp:935.
current_slot_selection.copy_semantics: getSave/putSave are whole-struct copies between dSv_info_c::mMemory (live) and mSavedata.mMemory[slot] (stored) - src/d/d_save.cpp:1506-1515.
current_slot_selection.consequence: Any two stages that share a slot share ALL of it: chest bits, memory switches, key count, big key, boss-dead. That is how a dungeon plus its miniboss room plus its boss room are one save state. See _stage_save_slots for the real, disc-derived assignment.

not_the_event_array.claim: Nothing on the dungeon-progression path touches dSv_event_c::mFlags[0x100] (include/d/d_save.h:696-710).
not_the_event_array.evidence: Every caller of onTbox/isTbox, on/off/isDungeonItem*, get/setKeyNum, on/isVisitedRoom and dComIfGs_on/off/isSwitch was grepped in src/; all of them route into dSv_memBit_c or dSv_danBit_c/dSv_zoneBit_c, never into mFlags.
not_the_event_array.one_exception: daMdoor ('Mori1', the sliding wooden bars) is the only door-family actor that uses story EVENT bits instead of switches - see _doors.Mori1.

per_stage_wrappers.note: For every accessor there is a dComIfGs_*(stageNo, ...) variant. It writes the live block when stageNo == GetSaveTbl(current stage), and otherwise writes the stored slot directly.
per_stage_wrappers.src: src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:694-895 (dComIfGs_onStageBossEnemy at :806-813 is the canonical shape)

routing.meaning: 'no switch' - on/off do nothing, is() returns FALSE

routing.persistence: PERSISTENT - saved to the memory card with the dungeon
VOLATILE - dSv_danBit_c::init(stageNo) clears both words whenever the save slot changes (src/d/d_save.cpp:1225-1235). Never written to the card.
VOLATILE and room-scoped; requires a valid roomNo 0..63 or the game asserts

_switch_numbers.why_it_matters: A locked door only stays unlocked if its switch number is < 0x80. dDoor_key2_c::keyInit guards on exactly that (src/d/d_door.cpp:436-437), and daDoor10_c::setKey short-circuits boss doors whose swbit >= 0x80 to 'locked' (src/d/actor/d_a_door10.cpp:44).

_stage_save_slots._how: Parsed from every stage's Stage.arc/stage.dzs STAG chunk on the retail GZLE01 disc: slot = (mProp>>1)&0x7F, key_counter_shown = mProp&1, stage_type = (mStageTypeAndSchbit>>16)&7. 156 stages carry a STAG chunk.
_stage_save_slots._confidence: high - this is read from the disc, and it agrees with the decomp's own slot names: the five stages that land in slots 3/4/5/6/7 are exactly M_NewD2 / kindan / Siren / M_Dai / kaze, matching STAGE_DRC / FW / TOTG / ET / WT.
_stage_save_slots._unused_slots: Slots 1 (STAGE_SEA2) and 14 (STAGE_BLUE_CHU_JELLY) belong to no stage on the disc. They are virtual, reached only through the dComIfGs_*Stage*(stageNo,..) wrappers: daTbox 'extra save info' chests write slot 1 (src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:318-323, :855-858) and Blue Chu Jelly pickups write switches in slot 14 (include/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.h:409-435).

_shared_param_layout.reason: all three derive from dDoor_info_c, and the actors themselves almost never read fopAcM_GetParam directly

getType.meaning: DOOR TYPE - the lock kind. Meaning differs per actor, see below.

getSwbit2.meaning: second switch, for the bars on the BACK side, 0xFF = none

rot_is_not_rotation.note: Only rot.y (home.angle.y) is a real rotation. rot.x and rot.z are packed data.

getArg1.meaning: model / behaviour variant, 0xFF = default. See each actor.

rot_is_not_rotation.cross_check: verified against the disc: every dungeon door's rot.x decodes to two room numbers that exist in that stage, and every plain door has rot.z low 6 bits == 0x3F

forced_boss_type.why_it_matters: This is how Earth Temple and Wind Temple get their Big-Key doors. Neither stage contains a single door20, and neither contains a door12 placed with type 3 in its params. Their boss doors are ordinary 'door12' placements whose rot.z high byte is 9 (M_Dai) or 12 (kaze), which the actor promotes to a boss door at runtime. Verified on the disc: M_Dai has exactly one such entry (params 0x0FFFF07F, rot.z 0x093F, swbit 0x7F) and kaze exactly one (params 0x0FFFF03F, rot.z 0x0C3F, swbit 0x3F).
forced_boss_type.confidence: high - the code is fully decompiled and the disc has exactly one matching placement per temple

open_gate.code: if (mKeyLock.mbEnabled) { case 3: if (!isDungeonItemBossKey()) return;  default: if (getKeyNum()==0) return; }

shape_from_arg1.note: shape 2 (arg1 9) and shape 5 (arg1 12) are the boss-door meshes, which is exactly why those two arg1 values force type 3

KDDOOR.decomp_status: STUB-ONLY - 342 lines in which EVERY function body is /* Nonmatching */. The header include/d/actor/d_a_kddoor.h still says '/* Place member variables here */' for all three classes, so even the field layout is unknown.
KDDOOR.confidence: low - nothing about this actor's behaviour can be stated from the decomp
what_is_known: it derives from dDoor_info_c (include/d/actor/d_a_kddoor.h:38), so it inherits the params / rot layout above
the stubbed method names mirror door10 exactly (chkMakeKey, setKey, chkMakeStop, chkStopF/B, chkStopOpen/Close, setEventPrm) plus two extras, chkGenocideCase and chkFeelerCase
one real literal survives: a collision cylinder r=15.0 h=300.0, AT_TYPE_UNK2000, dCcG_SE_WOOD (src/d/actor/d_a_kddoor.cpp:118-146)
what_is_NOT_known: which type values lock it, and whether it consumes keys at all
which model / archive it loads - getBmdName(), getBmdName2() and getDzbName() are all stubs (:190, :195, :200)
KDDOOR.retail_usage: only 9 placements in the whole game: 7 doorSH (all in kindan, all with params type nibble 3) and 2 doorKD (both in kindan, type nibble 0). For the remake, kindan's doorSH entries are the vine-covered Forbidden Woods doors.
KDDOOR.remake_advice: treat doorSH/doorKD as plain doors (no key) unless play-testing says otherwise - none of the 9 placements carries a small-key or boss-key type nibble under either door10's or door12's mapping

small_key.stored_in: dSv_memBit_c::mKeyNum, a u8 COUNT inside the current dungeon's save block - not a bit, not an event register
small_key.spend: dDoor_key2_c::keyInit(): if (!mbIsBossDoor) dComIfGp_setItemKeyNumCount(-1);  (src/d/d_door.cpp:438-439) - THE ONLY DECREMENT IN THE GAME

commit.code: if (ChkKeyDisp(stagInfo)) { if (pending != 0) { n = getKeyNum() + pending; clamp 0..99; setKeyNum(n); pending = 0; } ... }
commit.note: dComIfGs_setKeyNum has exactly ONE caller in the whole game: src/d/d_meter.cpp:5176. If the stage's STAG says keys are not displayed, the pending delta is never applied.

small_key.reset: dSv_memBit_c::init() sets mKeyNum = 0 (src/d/d_save.cpp:1067); the staging counter is zeroed at src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:80
remake_model: door prompt appears only if savedKeys > 0 (small) or hasBigKey (boss) AND the door's memory switch is not already set
unlock beat: if swbit < 0x80 set memory switch swbit (permanent); pendingKeys -= 1 for small keys only
each frame: savedKeys = clamp(savedKeys + pendingKeys, 0, 99); pendingKeys = 0
savedKeys, hasBigKey and memory switches 0x00-0x7F all live in the same per-dungeon block, so they all reset together when you enter a different dungeon

big_key.what_it_is: dSv_memBit_c::mDungeonItem bit 2 (BOSS_KEY) - a single flag in the dungeon's save block. There is no separate variable and no count.

never_consumed.claim: The Big Key is checked but never spent.
never_consumed.evidence: dDoor_key2_c::keyInit skips the decrement for boss doors (src/d/d_door.cpp:438). dComIfGs_offDungeonItemBossKey() exists (src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:785-792) but has NO caller anywhere in src/. It only clears when the whole block is re-initialised.

map.read: the only reader in the whole decompiled tree is item_getcheck_func_map() (src/d/d_item.cpp:2334-2337), which just answers 'do you already own it'

what_it_actually_changes.why: the dungeon map screen, src/d/d_menu_dmap.cpp, is 188 lines in which every one of the ~35 function bodies is /* Nonmatching */ - including screenSet(), initialize(), treasureSet(), treasureDraw() and dMap_isBossDoor(). Nothing in it is readable.
what_it_actually_changes.confidence: low on behaviour, high on the storage bit
what_can_be_said: the rooms you have walked through are tracked independently, in mVisitedRoom (see _storage), and dMap_c::mapMoveAll sets those bits whether or not you hold the map
so the standard Zelda reading - the map reveals unvisited rooms - is CONSISTENT with the data model, but is not proved by any line of code that could be read
each dungeon ships pre-rendered floor images in its Stage.arc as stage/dat/dmapNNN.png, one per FLOR entry; see _dungeons[].dungeon_map

_dungeons._how: doors are the TGDR chunk and chests the TRES chunk of each stage's Stage.arc/stage.dzs, re-parsed from the retail disc. Every dungeon's doors and chests live in the STAGE file, not the room files - all six stages have zero TGDR/TRE entries in any Room*.arc. 'lock' is derived by feeding each entry's real params through the decompiled getType()/chkMakeKey() of its actor, including door12's arg1 9/12 -> setType(3) promotion. 'eff_type' is the type after that promotion; 'type' is the raw nibble.

_field_notes.params: the raw u32 from the placement record
_field_notes.eff_type: type after daDoor12_c's arg1==9/12 -> setType(3) promotion
_field_notes.angle_y: the only real rotation, s16 binary angle (0x4000 = 90 deg)
_field_notes.open_switch: rot.z&0xFF, the switch the chest sets when opened, 255 = none

_cross_checks: Small-key doors vs small keys, per dungeon: M_NewD2 4 doors / 3 chest keys + 1 free-standing key item = 4. kindan 1 / 1. Siren 2 / 2. M_Dai 3 / 2 chest keys + 1 free-standing = 3. kaze 2 / 2. Every dungeon balances exactly.

Big-key doors, per dungeon: M_NewD2 1 (door20 type 1), kindan 1, Siren 1, M_Dai 1 (door12 arg1=9 promoted to type 3), kaze 1 (door12 arg1=12 promoted). ma2room 0. Each of the five real dungeons has exactly one 0x4E chest and exactly one big-key door.
Map + compass: every one of the six stages has exactly one 0x4C chest and one 0x4D chest.
Chest indices: tboxNo is unique within every dungeon and always < 32, so one u32 mTbox per slot is sufficient - checked on all six.
Door room pairs: every dungeon door's rot.x decodes to two room numbers that exist in that stage (verified independently against stage_data.json room lists).
The disc TGDR/TRES entries match the build's out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json entry for entry (same actor names, params and rot triples, chunk 'TGDR'/'TRES').
_gotchas: Cave08 is a leftover/partial COPY of Wind Temple data: it sits in save slot 7 (STAGE_WT) with keyDisp=1, has 14 door12 entries whose rot.x room pairs reference kaze's rooms (which Cave08 does not have), and carries its own 0x4C/0x4D/0x4E/2x0x15 chest set. Do not treat it as a real dungeon; do not let it write slot 7.

The model paths in stage_data.json for doors are unreliable - the resolver picks the first archive on the disc that happens to contain a matching BDL, so kindan's door10 entries point at res/Stage/Xboss1/... and M_NewD2's at res/Stage/Cave01/.... Per the decomp the mesh must come from the CURRENT stage's own Stage archive (dComIfG_getStageRes("Stage", getBdlName()), src/d/actor/d_a_door10.cpp:265) except for the arg1 13/14 DoorBs overrides.

The OBJNAME 'argument' column (e.g. door12=0, door12M=1, keyS12=1, ZenS12=2) is never read by any door actor - grepped all 8 door .cpp files, zero hits. Shape comes from arg1 (rot.z high byte); lock comes from the type nibble in params. Do not key remake behaviour off the placement name alone.
door10 and door12 use DIFFERENT type numbers for the same concept: door10 small=4/5 boss=1, door12 small=1 boss=3.

Doors placed in a BOSS or MINIBOSS stage are excluded from the dungeon-map door list: dStage_KeepDoorInfoProc returns early for stage types BOSS and MINIBOSS, and caps at 0x40 doors (src/d/d_stage.cpp:83-110, dStage_KeepDoorInfo at include/d/d_stage.h:979-986).

ma2room (Forsaken Fortress 2nd visit) has 17 door10 placements and ALL of them are plain type 0 with swbit 0xFF. It has no locked doors, no small keys and no big key - only a map and a compass chest. Its doors also have non-cardinal rot.y, unlike the other five dungeons.
_not_determined: What the MAP item visually changes. d_menu_dmap.cpp is 188 lines of pure /* Nonmatching */ stubs (every body, including screenSet, initialize, treasureSet, treasureDraw and dMap_isBossDoor). The storage bit is certain; the rendered effect is not readable. Confidence: low.

How the dungeon map decides a door is a boss door. dMap_isBossDoor(stage_tgsc_data_class*) exists at src/d/d_menu_dmap.cpp:25-27 and is a stub. It takes a raw TGDR record, so it almost certainly re-reads the type nibble - but that is an inference, not a read. Confidence: low.
What the COMPASS shows. Only the HUD-refresh trigger is decompiled (src/d/d_meter.cpp:4510-4519); the content is drawn by the stubbed dmap code. Confidence: low.

Everything about the KDDOOR actor (doorKD / doorSH / ZenshKD / K_ZshKD / doorSZ): its lock behaviour, its models, its member layout. src/d/actor/d_a_kddoor.cpp is 342 lines with every body stubbed and the header has no member variables at all. Confidence: low. Only the 9 retail placements (7 doorSH + 2 doorKD, all in kindan) and the inherited dDoor_info_c param layout are solid.
Whether mItem is 32 or 64 bits. The array is u32[1] but the assert says i < 64 (src/d/d_save.cpp:1112-1121). Unresolved in the decomp itself.

The meaning of the unnamed event flags the door code touches: dSv_event_flag_c::UNK_1101, UNK_1140, UNK_1704, UNK_1710, UNK_1B01, UNK_2601, UNK_2602 and dSv_event_tmp_flag_c::UNK_0440. The decomp has not named them.

Which floor image (dmapNNN.png) corresponds to which FLOR entry / floor number. The counts match per dungeon (kindan 5 FLOR / 5 images, M_Dai 3/3, kaze 3/3, M_NewD2 4/4, Siren 4/4) but the FLOR chunk itself was not decoded here.
How dSv_zone_c zones are assigned to rooms (dComIfGp_roomControl_getZoneNo) - only relevant if the remake wants zone-scoped switches (>= 0xC0); no dungeon door in the retail data uses one.
Whether the free-standing 'item' actors carrying id 0x15 in M_NewD2 and M_Dai are gated by anything (they are in stage_data.json but the gating flag was not traced).
